_: BATTLE BOTS / stable-diffusion lane C: THE PROMPT MATRIX. One table, read by scripts/sd/bots-sd-sweep.py, which enumerates it into runnable jobs and prices it. Nothing here is a taste list: every negative group below is named after a defect that has actually been produced by this project's own generations, and the axes are the knobs that plausibly move those defects. A blind grid over every parameter a sampler exposes would be 40 million renders and would still not answer the question.

skeleton._: Order matters in a CLIP-conditioned model: the first ~20 tokens dominate. So SUBJECT and VIEW come first, the finish and the light in the middle, and the plate last, because the plate is the part the ControlNet already settles. LENGTH: the assembled full prompt is 234 CLIP tokens (measured with the real tokenizer, 2026-09-05) against a 77-token context. Plain diffusers keeps the first 77 and silently deletes the rest, which is everything from `features` onward: the finish, the neutral law, the light law and the plate. So NOTHING sends this text to a model directly: scripts/sd/bots_sd_prompt.py assembles it, embeds it in full through compel in 77-token chunks, and weights the law clauses up (see `weights`). The matrix, the job files, the smoke test and the runner all read that one module.
skeleton._forehead: THE CLEAR FOREHEAD (lane H, 2026-09-05). `forehead` is carried by the head only (subject.head.forehead; bots_sd_prompt.segments() appends it after `features` for any slot whose subject entry carries the key, and no other slot does). Measured on the production heads: every design-2 pool (t1-2, t2-2, t3-2, t4-2) lost all 24 candidates, 20 to NO FACE and the 4 with a face to THIRD EYE plus MOUTH MISPLACED, with the dark feature always in the central band ABOVE the eye line (0.31 to 0.41 of head height down). The prompt never carried a family motif line; the feature comes from the design-2 placeholder, which is drawn as a cyclops (one big central lens on the forehead plus a ring or a slot on the crown) in public/bots-art/_raw/parts/placeholders/head-t*-2.png, and both control roots trace it. This clause and the `forehead` negative group are the prompt-side answer: the forehead is named as blank clay, the eyes as exactly two, and the family character is placed in the ear cups, the crown silhouette, the cheeks and the mouth grille, never above the eyes. MEASURED (lane H, the same day): with this clause and group, 72 renders of t2-2, t3-2 and t4-2 at the production recipe came back a cyclops on every one (70 NO FACE, plus 2 that rank-part passed only because the importer lit two tiny side nubs as the pair, eye radius 0.024 of head width against the 0.03 floor, a judge blind spot, not survivors); a second pass with the eye count in the first tokens, this clause at 1.40 and the negative led by 'a cyclops head, a single central lens, a robot with one eye' came back 36 NO FACE of 36. No wording beats a circle the lineart draws. The clause stays because it is right for a two-eyed placeholder; the placeholder fix is upstream of this file.

skeleton._viewShort: The terse variant exists to be the ONE arm that fits inside a single CLIP chunk, so it can prove whether chunking is helping or whether a short prompt plus a strong ControlNet is simply better. weights._: Per-clause compel weights, applied by scripts/sd/bots_sd_prompt.py build_weighted() and by nothing else. 1.0 is neutral; above 1.0 pulls the embedding toward that clause. These are the house laws that a 77-token cut used to delete outright, so they are embedded in full AND weighted up. Kept moderate: in practice weights past about 1.4 start to burn the image, and the ControlNet already holds the geometry so the prompt only has to win the register. Keys are skeleton segment names; a segment not listed here is 1.0. The plain prompt (no weights) is what the job files and the token counts report; the weighted form is what the model is fed. `forehead` is a head-only segment (see skeleton._forehead), so its weight touches no other slot.

subject._: One line per slot. Every one of them says ALONE, because the single commonest way to lose a part generation is for the model to draw the whole robot the part belongs to.  THE LEG SHAPES (lane B, 2026-09-05): `leg` is the dome boot and stays exactly as it was; `leg-wheels`, `leg-springs`, `leg-sneakers` and `leg-pegs` are the four new rulers scripts/bots-bake-parts.mjs --out v3 draws. They are keyed like slots because a slot key is what scripts/sd/bots_sd_prompt.py looks up, so a shape reaches the model with no code change, and each names its own coral part by its own word (tyre, pad, sole, pad) and says in its features clause that everything above that block is the body's own clay.

leg._: THE CORAL SOLE (2026-09-05). The production sweep asked for 'the shoe is a soft coral colour' and got, on 192 of 192 legs, a grey boot with coral rims along its panel lines, coral fills in the heel counter and the side port, and a grey plate under it; the judge rejected every one (NO SOLE, CORAL SPILL). The live legs and the concept boots carry the coral as ONE solid block at the bottom. So the clause names the block the v2 ruler draws in the coral material (a thick sole moulded under the boot, its own shape in the depth and lineart maps) and says where the coral is NOT. THE DOME BOOT (lane B, the same day): the second sweep held the sole on three legs and lost the other five to CORAL SPILL, every time on the boot's side pods (design 2) or its bands (bulldozer), which the render painted coral. So the form clause now names the shape the v2 ruler draws (a short cylinder ankle, a rounded dome boot, one coral sole block that never sticks out wider than the boot) and the features clause says in so many words that everything above the sole is the body's own clay, pods and bands included. The matching negative group is `coral` in negative.groups, carried by the leg in negative.slot.

leg-wheels._: WHEELS (lane B, 2026-09-05). One wheel a side. The coral is the TYRE and the tyre is the block the wheel STANDS IN, never a ring round the hub: rank-part.py measures the coral the importer will ship against the run of bottom rows where coral covers half the row's ink, so a ring reads to it as exactly the rim-and-drips defect that rejected 192 of 192 production legs. WAVE TWO (lane L, 2026-09-05). CORAL SPILL was the first rule to fire on 68 of wave one's 96 leg candidates, and the spill was not drips: the median candidate carried its coral 16 rows ABOVE the block in ONE unbroken blob, running straight on up the body. Sorted per shape it tracked exactly one number, the body's width over the block's width at the line where they meet (pegs 0.22 spilled 0.015, springs 0.72 spilled 0.047, wheels 1.00 spilled 0.075, sneakers 1.00 spilled 0.122), so the rulers now stand every body ON its block and the depth map stands the block up as its own slab. These clauses say the same thing in words: the block STEPS OUT PAST the body, and the thing directly above the block, the one a spill lands on, is named as clay in the same breath. The wheel is now a WHOLE circle whose bottom is buried in the tyre, so its hub clears the coral by 11 px and the form clause can say hub and circle without inviting a coral ring.

leg-springs._: SPRINGS. A clay coil on a coral pad. The turns are named CLAY twice, because the v2 sweep lost five legs of eight to CORAL SPILL on exactly this kind of repeated feature (the boot's side pods and its bands came back coral). The negative also forbids the gaps a drawn helix would leave, which the judge would read as SEE THROUGH. WAVE TWO (lane L, 2026-09-05). CORAL SPILL was the first rule to fire on 68 of wave one's 96 leg candidates, and the spill was not drips: the median candidate carried its coral 16 rows ABOVE the block in ONE unbroken blob, running straight on up the body. Sorted per shape it tracked exactly one number, the body's width over the block's width at the line where they meet (pegs 0.22 spilled 0.015, springs 0.72 spilled 0.047, wheels 1.00 spilled 0.075, sneakers 1.00 spilled 0.122), so the rulers now stand every body ON its block and the depth map stands the block up as its own slab. These clauses say the same thing in words: the block STEPS OUT PAST the body, and the thing directly above the block, the one a spill lands on, is named as clay in the same breath. Wave one's spill on this shape sat in the shadow BETWEEN the turns, which is why the features clause now says every turn and every shadow between them is clay.

leg-sneakers._: SNEAKERS. A shoe with a tongue on a coral sole. The tongue and the collar are named as clay because they are the two features nearest the coral block and so the two a render would most readily paint with it. Laces, eyelets and stripes are forbidden because each is a thin warm line the importer's pin_coral would pin and the judge would then read as spill. WAVE TWO (lane L, 2026-09-05). CORAL SPILL was the first rule to fire on 68 of wave one's 96 leg candidates, and the spill was not drips: the median candidate carried its coral 16 rows ABOVE the block in ONE unbroken blob, running straight on up the body. Sorted per shape it tracked exactly one number, the body's width over the block's width at the line where they meet (pegs 0.22 spilled 0.015, springs 0.72 spilled 0.047, wheels 1.00 spilled 0.075, sneakers 1.00 spilled 0.122), so the rulers now stand every body ON its block and the depth map stands the block up as its own slab. These clauses say the same thing in words: the block STEPS OUT PAST the body, and the thing directly above the block, the one a spill lands on, is named as clay in the same breath. This shape spilled the most of the four (0.122 at the median, 17 of 24 rejected) and it drew the spill as a SECOND COLOURED BAND above the sole, a mudguard. The ruler now insets the upper from the sole on both sides, so there is a step where that band used to sit.

leg-pegs._: PEGS. A thin peg on a round coral pad. The pad is the widest thing on the part and the peg the thinnest, and that IS the silhouette: at ring size a peg leg is read by the gap either side of the shaft, so the form clause says thin twice and says the pad is much wider than the peg. Sorted per shape it tracked exactly one number, the body's width over the block's width at the line where they meet (pegs 0.22 spilled 0.015, springs 0.72 spilled 0.047, wheels 1.00 spilled 0.075, sneakers 1.00 spilled 0.122), so the rulers now stand every body ON its block and the depth map stands the block up as its own slab. axes._: Ranges, with the reason each one is a range rather than a number. Cardinalities here are what scripts/sd/bots-sd-sweep.py multiplies.

checkpoint._: Screened in stage 1 and then fixed. Licences are recorded in the sweep script and every one of them needs confirming on the model card before anything ships.

controlStack._: THE question of this whole lane. Depth carries the form and the accent relief; lineart and canny carry the boundaries. Depth alone tends to soften a seam; canny alone lets the model invent the interior; the pair is the expected winner and has to be shown to be. `values` is the whole axis and the head's; `slot` below narrows it for the other four slots and carries the measurement that did so.

slot._: MEASURED 2026-09-05 on the v2 limb slice (stage1d-limbs-v2.jsonl: arm-t2-1, leg-t2-1, weapon-t2-1 and torso-t2-1 against the v2 control maps with the slot negatives, 64 renders, lineart against depth+lineart at control 0.7 and 0.85, adapter 0.3 and 0.45 on bot-2). Lineart ALONE at adapter 0.3 often came back as an OUTLINE DRAWING: a white fill with black lines and no shading, so no volume at all (the arm sheet, row two, columns one, two, five and six; the torso sheet, row two, several). Depth plus lineart never did. The judge has a blind spot for exactly this: after the as-shipped normalisation to neutral clay a flat white outline is uniform clay with a perfect silhouette overlap and nothing to repair, so rank-part ranked an outline drawing FIRST for the arm (composite 90.0) and high for the torso, where a person rejects it on sight. So lineart alone is off the arm, the leg, the weapon and the torso. Each carries the three stacks listed, depth alone, depth plus lineart and depth plus lineart plus canny, every one of them with the depth map that puts the volume in. depth+canny is not on the limb list either: it was not in the measured slice and the limb list is the three named; it stays on the head's axis. The head is absent from this map on purpose and keeps `values` whole: an outline was not measured on it and its slice files belong to another lane. bots-sd-sweep.py reads this map for the stage-1 product and for the limb slices (a job for a slot never carries a stack outside its list, and the planned counts exclude them); the runner does not read it, it checks that the maps a job's stack names are on disk.

controlScale._: The one knob that answers 'parts out of place'. Under about 0.6 the model wanders off the silhouette; over about 1.1 it traces the placeholder and gives back grey clay with no finish at all. The useful band is narrow and it moves with the checkpoint, which is why it is swept and not set.

controlEnd._: Where in the denoise the control lets go. Ending early frees the last steps to put the vinyl finish on; ending late holds the geometry harder. This is the knob that trades 'exactly the right shape but it looks like the placeholder' against 'beautiful and the wrong shape'.

style._: IP-Adapter scale (ip-adapter-plus_sdxl_vit-h), fed a reference from art-src/sd/style/clean. Zero is the control arm. Measured by hand on the box on 2026-09-05 with a concept crop as the style image: at 0.4 (control 0.6) the head came back as warm pastel clay with chrome bezels, a coral lit lens, the grille mouth and the ear cups, with the shape still bound; at 0.8 the reference photo's background (a crowd, a corkboard) leaked into the render. So the band is 0.3 to 0.6, the references have their backgrounds removed, and 0.7 is gone.

styleRef._: Which cleaned reference the adapter sees (art-src/sd/style/clean/<name>.png, made by bots-sd-stylerefs.py from the concept art; the manifest there says what each one is good for). A whole robot carries proportions and finish, a head carries the face. Names, not paths: the sweep resolves them and the runner refuses a name with no file.

promptVariant._: terse is subject+view+plate only; full is the whole skeleton; tier adds the richness clause. A long prompt fights a strong ControlNet for the same decisions, and which wins is measurable.

layout._: single letterboxes one part into the square; sheet packs a kit or a slot row onto one canvas at one shared scale. See bots-sd-controls.py: an arm alone fills 40 percent of a square frame and the model has the rest to invent in, while a sheet enforces one camera and one light across parts by construction and scores several parts per render.

gateTargets._: What the scorer asks of a candidate, drawn from scripts/bots-art-check.mts and rig-points.ts rather than invented, plus the three this lane adds. A candidate failing any HARD row is discarded before a person ever sees it.
